source.title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity

accepted.question_text: Given an asymptotically flat Einstein initial data set (M,g,K) and a future trapped surface Sigma, where a closed spacelike 2-surface is future trapped when both future null evolutions are area-non-increasing, must there exist a smooth spherical apparent horizon outside Sigma, meaning a surface with one future null mean curvature equal to zero?

evidence.quote: show there is a (smooth, spherical) apparent horizon outside

accepted.question_text: Given an asymptotically flat Einstein initial data set (M,g,K) and a future trapped surface Sigma, must there exist an apparent horizon inside Sigma, meaning a closed spacelike 2-surface with one future null mean curvature equal to zero?

evidence.quote: show there is an apparent horizon inside

accepted.question_text: For apparent horizons in spacelike hypersurfaces, to what extent is the analogy with minimal surfaces valid, and is there a meaningful second-variation or stability theory for the apparent-horizon equations despite the absence of a known functional whose Euler-Lagrange equations are the apparent-horizon equations?

evidence.quote: To what extent is this analogy valid?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an asymptotically flat vacuum Einstein initial data set, diffeomorphic to R^3, that contains an apparent horizon?
Does there exist an asymptotically flat scalar-flat Riemannian metric on R^3 that contains a minimal 2-sphere, and can the minimal 2-sphere be chosen to be stable?
Does an apparent horizon persist under Einstein evolution of the initial data set, or can one exhibit an explicit counterexample to persistence?
For a conformally flat asymptotically flat metric g = phi^4 delta with nonnegative scalar curvature, what conditions on the conformal factor phi guarantee that g has no horizon?

If M is an asymptotically flat 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and Sigma is a stable minimal 2-sphere in M, prove the Penrose inequality area(Sigma) <= 16*pi*(ADM mass)^2, and formulate and prove a corresponding inequality for initial data sets that are not time-symmetric.

For compact M, determine conditions on conformal data (gamma, A, tau), where gamma is a Riemannian metric, A is a traceless divergence-free symmetric tensor, and tau is a nonconstant mean-curvature function, that ensure solvability of the Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York system for (phi,W) with phi > 0.

evidence.quote: ensure the LCBY system is solvable

accepted.question_text: What asymptotic conditions allow the conformal method to construct Einstein initial data sets on an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold, such as a constant-mean-curvature hypersurface meeting future null infinity, thereby producing hyperboloidal initial data?

evidence.quote: construct initial data sets on an asymptotically hyperbolic manifold

accepted.question_text: Which hyperboloidal initial data arise from a spacetime with smooth conformal null infinity, and what class of Lichnerowicz-Choquet-Bruhat-York conformal data constructs such hyperboloidal initial data?

Classify the possible smoothness properties of hyperboloidal initial data at conformal infinity, and identify the weakest such conditions under which a positivity proof for the Bondi mass can be completed.

Can the space of globally hyperbolic vacuum Einstein metrics on V = R x M^3 have more than one connected component, and in the asymptotically flat setting with maximal Cauchy surfaces can one establish a compactness or Palais-Smale condition for the ADM mass function?
accepted.context_brief: Connected components of Einstein metric spaces

accepted.question_text: Under what conditions on the stress-energy tensor must a static asymptotically flat spacetime metric be spherically symmetric, especially in the perfect-fluid case known as the static star conjecture?
Find a good local characterization of the Kerr solution among stationary metrics, preferably one that is independent of the choice of slicing.
Suppose two disjoint Cauchy surfaces in an asymptotically flat vacuum spacetime carry isometric initial data. Must the spacetime be stationary, meaning that it admits a timelike Killing vector field?

Give a general description of the types of singularities that can occur in solutions of the static and stationary vacuum Einstein equations, beginning with the possible singularities of their spacelike slices.
accepted.context_brief: Singularities of static or stationary vacuum equations

accepted.question_text: Prove the existence of nonsingular asymptotically flat static spherically symmetric solutions of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations.
Show that there is no static spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills solution with nonzero electric field.
Analyze the time-dependent spherically symmetric Einstein-Yang-Mills equations, analogously to the known analysis of the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field equations.
Find axially symmetric static or stationary Einstein-Yang-Mills solutions that generalize the Kerr-Newman solution.

evidence.quote: axially symmetric static or stationary solutions

accepted.question_text: Find an Einstein-Yang-Mills analogue of the Majumdar-Papetrou superposition of extremal Reissner-Nordstrom solutions.
Show that every static black-hole solution of the Einstein-Yang-Mills equations must be Reissner-Nordstrom, equivalently that static Einstein-Yang-Mills black holes have no Yang-Mills hair.
accepted.context_brief: No hair for EYM black holes

accepted.question_text: For the vacuum Einstein equations, prove a theorem saying that if an approximate metric g_e has Ricci curvature small in a suitable norm, then there exists an exact Ricci-flat metric g close to g_e in that norm.
Show that a solution of the Einstein equations linearized about Minkowski space is close to a non-flat exact solution of the full Einstein equations.
Give precise conditions under which post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions converge to, or at least approximate, a global solution of the Einstein equations.
Prove the existence of a limit in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

Find a simple usable approximation scheme that accurately determines the gravitational radiation produced by an isolated astrophysical system, and in particular prove the quadrupole radiation formula.
Show that very small but finite test bodies move on spacetime geodesics.

In what sense does a Regge spacetime, modeled as a piecewise linear manifold with piecewise linear metric data, approximate a smooth vacuum spacetime, and what analogous convergence statement holds for numerical-relativity spacetimes?
Devise a numerical or lattice evolution scheme for the Einstein equations that can be proved to preserve the constraint equations, as a step toward proving convergence to a long-time solution.
Prove a uniqueness theorem for maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces assuming only the dominant energy condition, rather than the timelike convergence condition or existence of a timelike Killing field.

Generalize the maximal-surface estimates to show existence of a constant-mean-curvature hypersurface asymptotic to a prescribed cut of future null infinity in an asymptotically flat spacetime, and determine the weakest asymptotic conditions on null infinity under which this holds.
If an asymptotically flat spacetime has a Cauchy surface without horizons, must the spacetime contain a maximal Cauchy hypersurface?
Show that a maximal surface in a boost-type domain is necessarily asymptotically flat and coincides with the known maximal slices constructed in that setting.
Is there a timelike geodesically complete, inextendible Lorentzian manifold satisfying an energy condition and containing a partial Cauchy surface with a trapped surface?

Show that a weak Cauchy surface, defined as a pointwise limit of Cauchy surfaces, in a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying suitable energy conditions cannot contain an inextendible null geodesic.

Show that if condition (G) fails, or if there is a hidden infinity, in a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition, then the spacetime contains a trapped surface; thereby prove that such a cosmological spacetime is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R x M and is static.
Prove a singularity theorem assuming the dominant energy condition rather than the timelike convergence condition.

For continuous or Holder-continuous Lorentzian metrics, are length-maximizing timelike geodesics unique, what physical meaning would nonuniqueness of the timelike geodesic initial-value problem have, and should such nonuniqueness count as a spacetime singularity?

Prove a long-time existence theorem for the asymptotically flat vacuum Einstein equations in maximal slicing gauge, strong enough for large data to rule out globally naked singularities and shield formed singularities behind maximal-surface barriers.

Determine conditions on asymptotically flat initial data that ensure the null infinity of the resulting Einstein initial-value evolution is regular enough for the Penrose extended manifold to exist with at least a C^3 metric and for the peeling theorem to hold.
accepted.context_brief: Regular null infinity from AF data

accepted.question_text: Construct an exact purely radiative vacuum spacetime, or prove existence of one, with complete smooth past and future null infinities, regular timelike infinities, and positive mass.

Find the weakest possible regularity assumptions under which a Lorentzian metric can be considered a vacuum solution of the Einstein equations, including the distributional case where the metric and inverse are essentially bounded and first derivatives are square-integrable, and determine the optimal coordinates or differentiable structure for such a metric.

Are there regularity conditions for the vacuum Einstein initial-value problem that guarantee existence but not uniqueness, and is there smooth initial data whose vacuum evolution develops a singularity after which it can be extended nonuniquely while preserving global hyperbolicity?
Prove long-time existence in constant-mean-curvature slicing gauge for cosmological vacuum spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces.

Prove that every globally hyperbolic maximally extended solution of the Einstein or Einstein-Maxwell equations on V = R x S^3 contains a maximal hypersurface and both a big bang and a big crunch; equivalently, decide whether any such vacuum or Einstein-Maxwell solution fails to admit a constant-mean-curvature foliation, including the Bianchi IX special case.
accepted.context_brief: Maximal slices and CMC foliations on R x S3

accepted.question_text: Show that spacetime metrics that are smoothly or distributionally extendible across Cauchy horizons form a measure-zero subset of all spacetimes, in an appropriate sense.
Find an exact solution of the Einstein equations representing two orbiting bodies, and determine whether the two-body system is unstable in Einstein gravity.
Determine the class of spacetimes that are asymptotically velocity dominated near a singularity, in a suitably defined sense.

Show that the only vacuum Robinson-Trautman solution on S^2 x R with positive mass is the Schwarzschild metric, and determine whether an analogous theorem holds for the Einstein-Maxwell Robinson-Trautman equations.
Prove that perturbations of the Schwarzschild and Kerr black-hole solutions decay exponentially, establishing black-hole stability in the sense suggested by physical and linearized arguments.
Show that if a cosmological spacetime has constant-mean-curvature initial data with positive Ricci 3-curvature, then the Einstein evolution preserves Ricci positivity.

Find a sensible notion of quasi-local mass that appears in nontrivial theorems, for example a theorem asserting that if a 3-dimensional region of volume V has quasi-local mass above a threshold M0(V,...), then every spacetime containing that region must contain a trapped surface and hence a black hole.

Show that the class of asymptotically flat 3-manifolds satisfying the hypotheses of the positive mass theorem has a weak compactness property, such as convergence of subsequences with bounded mass and bounded geometry, and determine the expected regularity of the limiting manifold.

Given a bounded region Q with connected boundary inside an asymptotically flat 3-manifold satisfying the positive mass theorem hypotheses, show that Q has an isometric extension by another such manifold that is static outside Q; further, determine whether the static extension has least ADM mass among horizon-free extensions outside Q.
Construct a proof of the positive mass theorem based on Geroch's idea of foliating by 2-spheres, including the existence of the special foliations required by that argument.
accepted.context_brief: Geroch foliation proof of positive mass

accepted.question_text: Show that Bartnik quasi-local mass is strictly positive for non-flat data, and show that Penrose quasi-local mass is nonnegative on reasonable data.
Explain the relationship between the various proposed definitions of quasi-local mass in general relativity.

trace.notes: The original zbMATH URL was blocked by a Cloudflare challenge in local curl. Local shard metadata identified the record as Robert Bartnik, Some open problems in mathematical relativity, and exact-title recovery found the ANU CMA proceedings page linking the chapter PDF used for extraction. Local curl could not download the ANU PDF because DNS resolution is disabled in the sandbox, but the PDF was readable through the page/PDF reader.

Mapped a 25-page PDF chapter. Open-problem regions are organized under Apparent Horizons; Initial Data Sets; Uniqueness/Rigidity Theorems; Approximations; Maximal and Prescribed Mean Curvature Surfaces; Causality and Singularities; Initial Value Problem (Cosmic Censorship); and Quasi-Local Mass.
Extracted 59 explicit bullet or sub-bullet research questions from the mapped open-problem regions. Solved-status labels were not present in the source.

Rewrote all accepted items as standalone mathematical-relativity questions, expanding local abbreviations such as AF, CMC, IVP, TCC, DE, EYM, and QL mass where supported by the surrounding source text.
No near-duplicate merges were applied; subquestions in the Einstein-Yang-Mills and cosmic-censorship sections were retained as distinct problems because the source lists them as separate tasks.
Accepted 59 self-contained items with page-located evidence anchors. Evidence quotes are intentionally short source anchors rather than extended verbatim problem statements.
